subject: physical-education
title: Guided practice B: sharing a short sequence by choice
focus: sharing a short sequence by choice
essentialQuestion: How does movement fit with beat, tempo, and expression?
standards: Michigan PE Standard 1: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns
Michigan PE Standard 2: Applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and physical activities
Michigan PE Standard 5: Recognizes the value of physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression and/or other benefits

lessonFamilyPlan.instructionalPurpose: create or communicate an inclusive activity response
lessonFamilyPlan.guidedEmphasis: Model the role, consent or space rule, inclusive choice, and cue-based feedback separately.
lessonFamilyPlan.independentEvidence: Create a fresh solo sequence or briefing that includes the same access and safety choices.
lessonFamilyPlan.evidencePurpose: communication, inclusion, creative sequence, planning, and completion

goal: I can create or communicate an inclusive activity response for sharing a short sequence by choice, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Count, shape, change, finish. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Repeat one small movement on a steady four-count.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: quiet music or a rhythm source.
Count, clap, tap, sign, or use an internal beat.
movementCues: Sharing is always the performer choice.
You may show it to one trusted adult only.
Describing the sequence counts as fully as performing it.
Give feedback about the movement, never about the person.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Use one short action at a time, say the main cue before the attempt, keep the cooperative creative activity choice concrete, and ask a trusted adult to confirm any required permission or space check.

movementModel.title: Model for sharing a short sequence by choice
movementModel.startingPosition: Choose a stable seated, supported, standing, or described position inside one arm-span.
movementModel.action: Count four comfortable beats, make one repeatable shape, change one feature, and finish under control.
movementModel.commonError: Assuming everyone will perform for the group. Fix: offer describe, show to one adult, or opt out, as equal options from the start.
movementModel.correction: Return to one small shape and one change, use a slower internal count, and mark the finish.
movementModel.notice: Notice timing, clear change, and controlled transition rather than copying body shape.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice timing, clear change, and controlled transition rather than copying body shape.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Keep every movement within a comfortable range and personal boundary; use the described route if the surface or space is uncertain. No lift, inversion, forced contact, unfamiliar acrobatics, public performance, or movement beyond personal space.

guidedPractice.prompt: Model the role, consent or space rule, inclusive choice, and cue-based feedback separately. Repeat one small movement on a steady four-count. Apply it to sharing a short sequence by choice.
guidedPractice.support: Use the model cue: Count, shape, change, finish.
guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Return to one small shape and one change, use a slower internal count, and mark the finish.

guidedPractice.prompt: Add one clear shape change while keeping the same count.
guidedPractice.support: Watch for this contrast: Adding several changes so the sequence loses its beat or safe boundary.
guidedPractice.feedback: Keep the safe version when the learner can show or explain notice timing, clear change, and controlled transition rather than copying body shape.

practiceProgression.name: Entry version
practiceProgression.task: Model the role, consent or space rule, inclusive choice, and cue-based feedback separately. Add one clear shape change while keeping the same count.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Show or explain the target for sharing a short sequence by choice once with the safe boundary intact.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: None; begin with the simplest safe version.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Remain here, reduce range or pace, add support, rest, or switch to the described route.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No lift, inversion, forced contact, unfamiliar acrobatics, public performance, or movement beyond personal space.

practiceProgression.name: One change
practiceProgression.task: Add one clear shape change while keeping the same count. Then change only level, direction, shape, tempo, or order. Keep the communication, inclusion, creative sequence, planning, and completion purpose visible.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Name what changed and keep the same cue, control, decision, and safety boundary.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: Change only level, direction, shape, tempo, or order.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Progress only by choice; repeat or regress whenever the cue or control is not clear.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No lift, inversion, forced contact, unfamiliar acrobatics, public performance, or movement beyond personal space.

practiceProgression.name: Fresh application
practiceProgression.task: Create a fresh solo sequence or briefing that includes the same access and safety choices. Create a fresh short sequence with a clear start, one chosen change, and stable finish; then name how the choice fits the focus.
practiceProgression.successCheck: Complete the fresh bounded application and identify the cue or decision that controlled it.
practiceProgression.changedVariable: The learner selects a new safe example, arrangement, or condition.
practiceProgression.learnerChoice: Use any standard or equal-credit route, take breaks, or finish through description without penalty.
practiceProgression.maximumBoundary: No lift, inversion, forced contact, unfamiliar acrobatics, public performance, or movement beyond personal space.

independentActivity.title: Fresh application: sharing a short sequence by choice
directions: Create a fresh short sequence with a clear start, one chosen change, and stable finish; then name how the choice fits the focus.
Use this cue or decision: Count, shape, change, finish.
Provide the selected evidence without a recording or body metric.
independentActivity.freshTask: Create a fresh solo sequence or briefing that includes the same access and safety choices. Create a fresh short sequence with a clear start, one chosen change, and stable finish; then name how the choice fits the focus.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Tap or count a comfortable steady beat.
Rehearse the starting and finishing shapes at reduced range.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Clear one arm-span on a non-slip surface or use one stable seat. No partner, audience, lift, inversion, throw, or public performance is required. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: quiet music or a rhythm source.
householdSubstitutes: Count, clap, tap, sign, or use an internal beat.
prohibited: No lift, inversion, forced contact, unfamiliar acrobatics, public performance, or movement beyond personal space.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit solo route: create, gesture, draw, or describe a four-count seated or standing sequence with a start, one change, and a stable finish.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Keep every movement within a comfortable range and personal boundary; use the described route if the surface or space is uncertain.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.seated: Use a stable seated position and preserve the Count, shape, change, finish. evidence through upper-body movement, pointing, gesture, object modeling, or description.
adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for sharing a short sequence by choice, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for sharing a short sequence by choice.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Count, shape, change, finish. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit solo route: create, gesture, draw, or describe a four-count seated or standing sequence with a start, one change, and a stable finish.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit solo route: create, gesture, draw, or describe a four-count seated or standing sequence with a start, one change, and a stable finish.
adaptationRoutes.describedOrDecisionRoute: Describe, draw, gesture, point, sign, or model Create a fresh short sequence with a clear start, one chosen change, and stable finish; then name how the choice fits the focus. This is a complete equal-credit route when movement is not appropriate.

accessibleAdaptation: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice timing, clear change, and controlled transition rather than copying body shape. The standard route is never required and adaptation never lowers credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit solo route: create, gesture, draw, or describe a four-count seated or standing sequence with a start, one change, and a stable finish.
activitySteps: Choose a standard or equal-credit response route.
Read the STOP AND TELL rule.
Complete the warm-up when it applies.
Use the safe finish when it applies.
Answer the short reflection or leave it blank.
commonErrorToWatchFor: Assuming everyone will perform for the group. Fix: offer describe, show to one adult, or opt out, as equal options from the start.

learnerEvidence: One guided response using Count, shape, change, finish..
One fresh bounded application or complete described equivalent for sharing a short sequence by choice.
One cue, decision, safety, or next-step explanation.
evidenceExpectations.observer: A learner may self-check a cue and a trusted human may review the selected evidence. A Tutor, browser, camera, wearable, or self-report cannot certify physical completion, guardian permission, or safe return.
doNotCollect: weight, appearance, body composition, calories, body shape, fitness norms, speed versus peers, or athletic talent
diagnosis, disability reason, symptom history, or private medical information
photo, video, audio, wearable data, location proof, or exercise log

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for sharing a short sequence by choice; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Repeat one small movement on a steady four-count.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Count, shape, change, finish.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Adding several changes so the sequence loses its beat or safe boundary. — with this correction — Return to one small shape and one change, use a slower internal count, and mark the finish.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Add one clear shape change while keeping the same count.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Create a fresh short sequence with a clear start, one chosen change, and stable finish; then name how the choice fits the focus. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice timing, clear change, and controlled transition rather than copying body shape. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.

coach how the learner presents their own evidence
route to rest, stop, retry, or adult handoff

cannot claim unapproved observation or certify physical completion
cannot override rest, stop, adaptation, guardian authority, professional authority, or safe return

knowledgeCheck: State the starting position, action, key cue, common error, and correction for sharing a short sequence by choice. Then distinguish optional REST / ADJUST from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME.
completionCriteria: The learner uses a safe setup or accurately describes it for sharing a short sequence by choice.
The learner applies Count, shape, change, finish. in one guided attempt and one fresh application or complete described equivalent.
The learner distinguishes learner-controlled rest from STOP AND TELL and DO NOT RESUME conditions.
Any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route earns equal credit for the same cue or decision evidence.
adaptationChoices: Choose or change any seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, mobility-aid, solo, low-space, no-equipment, or described route without explaining why. Every route earns equal credit for the same notice timing, clear change, and controlled transition rather than copying body shape. extensionChallenge: Apply sharing a short sequence by choice under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Which cue, decision, safety check, or adaptation preserved the target for sharing a short sequence by choice, and what would you keep or change in a next safe attempt?

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
